beats.intro: Some conditions come in pairs. A ride might require you to be at least one hundred twenty centimeters tall and at most one hundred ninety. [[q]]Two inequalities joined together make a compound inequality.
beats.and: When two inequalities are joined by and, a solution must make both of them true. [[q]]Take x is at least negative one, and x is at most four. [[g1]]Graph the first one: everything from negative one to the right. [[g2]]Graph the second: everything from four to the left. [[over]]The solution is where the two graphs overlap: [[seg]]all the numbers from negative one to four, both included. [[write]]You can write this as negative one is less than or equal to x, which is less than or equal to four.
beats.andEdge: Two things can happen with and. [[q]]For x is greater than zero, and x is at least negative three, [[inside]]one ray sits inside the other, so the overlap is just x greater than zero. [[q2]]For x is greater than two, and x is less than negative four, [[none]]the rays point away from each other. They never overlap, [[ans]]so there is no solution.
beats.or: When two inequalities are joined by or, a solution only needs to make at least one of them true. [[q]]Take x is less than negative two, or x is at most negative one. [[g1]]Graph each one. [[union]]Put the two graphs together. Everything shaded in either graph is a solution. [[ans]]Together they cover x is at most negative one. [[q2]]And for x is greater than zero, or x is less than two, [[all]]the two rays together cover the whole number line: every real number is a solution.
beats.interval: There's a short way to write these sets, called interval notation. [[br]]A square bracket means the endpoint is included, like a closed circle. [[pa]]A round parenthesis means it is not included, like an open circle. [[ex]]So negative three is less than or equal to x, which is less than two, is written square bracket negative three, comma, two, round parenthesis. [[inf]]A ray that never ends uses the infinity symbol, always with a round parenthesis, because infinity is not a number you can reach: x at least negative three is square bracket negative three, comma, infinity. [[all]]All real numbers are negative infinity to infinity, [[empty]]and no solution is the empty set.
beats.wrap: A compound inequality joins two inequalities. [[w1]]With and, keep only the overlap. It can be empty. [[w2]]With or, keep everything in either graph. It can be all numbers. [[w3]]In interval notation, brackets include the endpoint, parentheses don't, and infinity always gets a parenthesis. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
